title: Glossary
intro: Sanskrit and Hindi terms with plain explanations.
editorialNote: Editorial content authored for this app. It has not been through independent scholarly review. See the Content Verification page.

terms.definition: The gesture of the raised open palm meaning 'do not fear'.
The half-female form of Shiva; tradition says Shiva attained it through the Goddess's grace.
A bolt or bar; the name of the auxiliary hymn recited with the Saptashati.
The offset between tropical and sidereal zodiacs. Traditions differ in which is used, which is why panchangs can disagree.
Food offered to the deity and later distributed as prasad.
A seed syllable in a mantra, such as aim, hrim, klim. Not lexical words.
The name the Devi Mahatmya uses most often for its Goddess.
Recitation of the Durga Saptashati.
A narrative cycle. The Saptashati has three.
A small hourglass drum, associated with Shiva and with Mahagauri.
Meditation; also the descriptive verse recited before visualising a deity.
The Gujarati circle dance performed through the Navratri nights.
The installation of the kalash that opens Navratri.
One of the three qualities — sattva, rajas, tamas — that compose prakriti.
The ritual pot installed on the first day of Navratri.
Armour; the protective hymn recited first in the Navangam sequence.
A pin or wedge; the auxiliary hymn recited to remove obstacles to recitation.
Worship of young girls as forms of the Goddess, on Ashtami or Navami in many traditions.
The great illusion; a name of the Goddess in the Devi Mahatmya.
An auspicious time window. Location-specific, never universal.
One of the 27 lunar mansions.
The nine-part recitation sequence of the Saptashati used in many traditions.
The nine-syllable mantra of Chandika.
Ritual placement of mantra syllables on the body.
A lunar fortnight: shukla (waxing) or krishna (waning).
The five-limb Hindu calendar: tithi, vara, nakshatra, yoga, karana.
Continuous recitation of a text.
In the Vaishno Devi cave, the natural rock formations worshipped as the Goddess.
Food offered to the deity and then shared.
The Bengali rite at the junction of Ashtami and Navami.
The formal statement of intention made at the start of a rite.
Power, capacity, energy. In Shakta thought, the Goddess herself.
A sacred seat associated with a part of Sati's body. Lists differ.
A hymn of praise.
A lunar day, one twelfth of the Sun-Moon elongation cycle.
The three-part recitation method, one charitra per day.
The trident; represents the three gunas.
The gesture of the downward open palm meaning 'giving'.
A vow, often involving fasting.
A geometric diagram used in worship; Ambaji worships one aniconically.
The Goddess as the power of yoga and of illusion, named in ch. 1.
